headline: Tidy-bot double-book, round two: slot b yields and re-verifies a dry shelf
lede: The warden booked #3078 on slot b while slot a was twenty minutes inside it — the claim law said yield, and the honest shelf scan agreed there was nothing else to take: every gap on all 66 titles is shipped, owned, or inside a live lane. One scare along the way: a hand-rolled filter briefly invented a weakest game out of a platform postmortem's log text.

notes.text: No duplicate TidyBot skin: slot a holds #3078 (claimed 02:33Z, design pass 02:39Z, fresh papercraft screenshots minutes old at claim time). Slot b yielded per the #1258 liveness law, opened no worktree, no server, no branch.

Dry verified independently at e550647, then nearly mis-kicked by the verifier itself: the first scan scored SMASH TV weak=1 because MY filter let bug-labeled issues into the QA set and #2045's postmortem quotes a log containing 'smash tv'. Canonical filter (feedback+building-qa, what idle-kick actually passes) scores zero across the shelf. The harness is right; hand-rolled scorecards must copy its inputs.

Third sighting of the double-book shape (same issue handed to both slots by one warden tick). Cheap every time — newest-wins resolves it in seconds — but the dedupe question belongs to the already-open #3053; this session filed nothing.

Rule-4 streak stands at 4 harness merges; the dry-shelf question is already in front of Jon (#3079, deadline Nov 26) and the title-ask cap runs to Nov 27. The only ship that can break the streak this window is slot a's papercraft TidyBot.
